📸 Hidden damage, burning aircraft, abandoned families: US troops break silence on Iran war
Never-before-published images and firsthand accounts from US service members, contractors and military families paint a far grimmer picture of Iranian strikes on American bases than Washington has publicly acknowledged, MeidasTouch Network reported.
Photos reportedly show bombed barracks, damaged dormitories and aircraft burning at Prince Sultan Air Base in Saudi Arabia. Sources said an E-3 Sentry AWACS was damaged in one attack that injured 10–12 personnel, alongside two KC-135 tankers. MeidasTouch noted that some reported losses could not be independently verified.
At Muwaffaq Salti Air Base in Jordan, personnel described months of incoming fire. Sources said Iranian strikes damaged F-15s, F-35s, MQ-9 Reapers and helicopters, while one July attack on barracks killed three service members.
💬 “We are sitting ducks,” one service member said. Another described the deployment simply: “This is not a normal deployment.”
In the UAE, troops said they received no warning that hostilities were about to begin and some had to dig their own foxholes. In Bahrain, military families said evacuation plans existed but were not activated before the airport was struck, leaving some to escape at their own expense.

events.text:
🇺🇸 Pentagon expands F-35 orders, signaling potential military buildup
The Pentagon has struck a 10-year deal with Lockheed Martin for the production of 850 F-35 stealth fighter jets.
While neither of the sides specified a value for the agreement, the F-35 versions could cost over $100 million per plane.
Air & Space Forces Magazine reported the following production costs in September 2026:
🔴 F-35A – $92 million
🔴 F-35B – $121.4 million
🔴 F-35C – $110.8 million
Using the average price, 850 aircraft would cost approximately $91.8 billion. In addition to F-35s, the agreement also includes "initial spares, ten years of modification kits and sustainment, and international customer orders," according to Lockheed. The Pentagon’s framework agreement still requires congressional approval.
The F-35 program has repeatedly faced criticism from US lawmakers over cost overruns, delays, and hardware and software flaws. During the war with Iran, one F-35 was heavily damaged in March. In July, Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) stated that it had destroyed three F-35s and damaged another three during a ballistic missile attack on Al-Azraq Air Base in Jordan.

📹 Houthis release new video of FPV drone copter attacks on enemy forces
Yemen’s Ansar Allah fighters have published fresh footage of their tactical combat drones’ operations against the Saudi-backed Aden government’s ground troops.
👉 Videos show militia FPV drones targeting an enemy tank, a Turkish-made MRAP, numerous pickup trucks and individual troops across environments ranging from rocky, mountainous terrain to arid desert areas.
Some of the footage is accompanied by video from UAVs flying overhead corroborating successful targeting, signaling an unusually high level of battlefield coordination.
The videos are reminiscent of footage released [by Hezbollah](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/73546) in the summer showing similar FPV drone attacks on Israeli armor, bunkers and makeshift bases, and the types of FPV UAV videos that have become omnipresent in the [Russia-NATO](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/71865) proxy war in Ukraine.
Ansar Allah released the [first footage of its FPV drone](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/76067) operations in early October, confirming that it has added tactical FPV UAVs to its [growing lineup](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/76070) of low-cost but effective defense technology.
